name: audit5 review V4C: the upgrade from the real version 3 code to this build pins the whole storage and every holding to the byte, with vestings in every state (unclaimed, part claimed and stamped, cancelled, finished, a version 1 layout key, an EGLD vesting, a bounced key held by the contract, a surplus, fees accrued); each state then moves on under version 4

steps.comment: The code mainnet runs: scenarios/v3/mvxvest-v3.wasm, blake2b-256 65c689b9... (mainnet account code, 29,327 bytes). Payable (0502) only until the upgrade, so that a bounce can be emulated with a plain transfer back; mainnet is 0500 and the upgrade sets 0500. Vesting 1 is seeded as version 1 left it on mainnet (VESTKEY-f56bea-01: attributes without cancelable or metadata, a real URI), the rest is made by version 3 itself below.
Version 3: 3 and 4 pay 250 each and go back stamped, 5 is over and burns; one MultiESDTNFTTransfer of 1500 FOX and the two keys.
Version 3: vesting 4 stops at T0+500 with 500 vested (250 of it claimed) and 500 refunded.
What a cross-shard bounce leaves: bob (a contract that could not receive it, say) sends key 7 back to the contract with no call. The contract holds it.
A bounced payout: 7 FOX come back to the contract with no call. Surplus.
Before the upgrade: every storage entry, every holding, every balance. (Payable only so that the bounces above could be emulated with plain transfers: mx-scenario-go has no shards.)
The owner upgrades to this build, metadata 0500 as on mainnet.
After the upgrade: the same storage, holdings and balances to the byte; only the code and the metadata (0500 as on mainnet) changed.

steps.comment: The version 1 layout key, never stamped: pays 750, stamped with cancelable:0 and claimed:750 and no metadata, its URI kept; the 750 FOX and the key leave apart.
Right after, the same key pays nothing: version 4 refuses whole, nothing booked, the key comes back with the failure.

2 (unclaimed under v3) pays 750, 3 (stamped by v3) pays 500 and keeps its metadata, 4 (cancelled by v3) pays its last 250 and burns. One ESDTTransfer of 1500 FOX, one transfer of the two keys that go back.
The EGLD vesting made by v3 is cancelled under v4: 250 EGLD back to the creator in a plain value transfer, no built-in call.
Its claim key pays the 750 that had vested at the cancel and burns: only the value transfer, no key transfer.

steps.comment: The key version 3 held goes back to its holder.
The surplus of version 3 is still 7 and nothing more: the locked 2250 stay.
The 600 EGLD of fees accrued under version 3.

Every unit where it belongs. The contract keeps exactly what it still owes (250 each on vestings 1, 2 and 3) and no key; alice 1500 + 750 + 1500 FOX and the 750 EGLD; bob his 1000; the creator the 500 refund, the 7 back and the 250 EGLD; the owner the token fees and the 600 EGLD.
